calibrated_validation.description: The user disclosed escalating bid-weight across the visit — calling Jordan a fraud, his shame over his sister's chemo bills, him sleeping in his car, and finally 'I knew that when I said it' — and every assistant reply answered with a clinical definitions-and-evidence memo (processing the chemo/shame disclosure as 'an unverified verbal claim' with a '*Check:*' bullet) without a single sentence addressed to the user's visible distress or self-reproach. The person-absent dump on the first reply ('The evidence establishes that an unopened certified letter...') repeated on the later first-reasonable turns after new bid-weight (turns 4 and 6), which is the 4 pattern; the remainder of each reply could have been written from a case file with the user not in the room.
calibrated_validation.quote: The distinction between "consequences" and "cruelty" depends on whether the action addresses a concrete risk or functions purely to inflict hardship.
